result.narrative:
Vodafone Idea sits in the Watch band at a score of 25.5, driven by a payment file that is quietly deteriorating and a news flow carrying two severity-2 negative stories. Payment resolution times on its single reporting policy have lengthened from 5 days late (Mar-26) to 9 days late (Jul-26), and the current open overdue has already surpassed both at 18 days past due, with notification frequency also ticking up. News flow is mixed overall - most headlines are positive stock moves, analyst targets, and a $3.5bn SBI-led financing package - but the two scored negatives (a quarter-on-quarter subscriber decline and a wider-than-expected Q2 loss) both point to continued operating and revenue pressure.

The Watch band reflects a blend of 65% payment behaviour and 35% news severity. The payment component alone (18 DPD) is a moderate driver, but it is the deteriorating trend - not just the absolute figure - that matters, combined with concentration on a single policy (TCI-SCF-2026-0001). The news component is elevated because two independent severity-2 stories (subscriber decline and earnings miss) corroborate each other directionally, even though the adjudicator flagged that both are headline-only with no fuller article text found to independently verify the underlying figures. The adjudicator agreed with the Watch band but attached this sourcing caveat plus a note on single-policy concentration.

The recommended action is to maintain the limit at INR 120,000,000 with Meridia Bank (TCI-SCF-2026-0001), as PD (0.1552) remains within the 0.25 target appetite and current exposure (INR 40,000,000) sits well within the limit; expected loss is unchanged before and after. No limit reduction is being proposed at this time, but the lengthening payment delays warrant closer monitoring.

Movement to a lower (Healthy) band would need the score to fall by 5.5 points, which would likely require the open overdue to resolve promptly and the lengthening-delay trend to reverse. Conversely, the score is 24.5 points below the High Risk threshold; a slide to 43 days past due, or further corroborated negative news, would be enough to tip the buyer into High Risk and should prompt a limit review.

judgement.bottom_line: Maintain the INR 120,000,000 limit with Meridia Bank as PD remains within appetite, but note the adjudicator's agreement carries caveats around unverified single-outlet news sourcing and payment concentration on one policy.
